description:
Expand the existing NYC Taxi benchmark to support additional TLC data sources
beyond Yellow Taxi. The current implementation only covers Yellow Taxi trips,
but NYC TLC provides three additional data types that represent significant
portions of modern NYC mobility patterns.

This expansion would:
- Add Green Taxi (street hail livery) data support
- Add For-Hire Vehicle (FHV) data support
- Add High Volume For-Hire Vehicle (HVFHV) data for Uber/Lyft (since 2019)
- Enable comparative analytics across taxi types
- Provide more complete NYC mobility benchmarking

Current implementation: benchbox/core/nyctaxi/
- benchmark.py, schema.py, queries.py, downloader.py, spatial.py
- 25 OLAP queries + 18 spatial queries
- Scale factors: 0.01 to 100 (TPC-aligned: SF=1 ≈ 1GB)

anti_patterns.dont: change the Yellow Taxi schema column names
anti_patterns.instead: add new taxi type tables/columns alongside existing ones
anti_patterns.why: 25 OLAP queries depend on current column names

anti_patterns.dont: download real TLC data in unit tests
anti_patterns.why: files are 50MB+ per month and TLC rate-limits

anti_patterns.dont: merge all taxi types into one table
anti_patterns.instead: use separate tables or a discriminated union
anti_patterns.why: FHV has a fundamentally different schema (no fare breakdown)

deferrals.reason:
FHV has the simplest schema and lowest volume (~1M/month). Phased rollout
prioritizes Green (similar to Yellow) and HVFHV (highest volume) first.
FHV can be added as a follow-up once the multi-type framework is proven.
deferrals.summary: Add FHV data support (downloader, queries, tests)

work_units.notes:
Option B (single combined table) is ruled out by anti_pattern: FHV has a
fundamentally different schema with no fare breakdown.

Remaining options:
A) Separate tables per type (yellow_trips, green_trips, hvfhv_trips)
   + Simplest, no NULLable columns, each table matches source schema exactly
   + Existing Yellow queries untouched
   - Cross-type queries need UNION ALL
C) Common core table + type-specific extension tables
   + Cleaner cross-type queries (core table has shared columns)
   + Normalizes common fields (pickup/dropoff time, location IDs)
   - More complex schema, migration risk for existing Yellow data

Deliverable: ADR in notes or context_sections documenting the decision
and rationale, before any schema code is written.
work_units.summary: Decide schema approach - separate tables (option A) vs core+extensions (option C)
